purpose: Tier 2 retrieval evaluation: 25 arXiv cs.AI research questions used to measure nDCG@10, recall@10, MRR and P@10 for the retrieval configurations. They are retrieval questions, so 'relevant' means the paper helps answer it, not that the paper agrees with the funnel.
rule: Authored before any retrieval was run for this wave and never edited afterwards. A query added or reworded after seeing a ranking invalidates the metric it was measured on. The set covers the project's own subject area and the four question shapes the system is for: method, comparison, evaluation, and resource.

spread.comparison: how two or more approaches differ
spread.evaluation: how something is measured or what a result means
spread.resource: what exists: a dataset, benchmark or system

queries.text: What methods do language model systems use to aggregate information that exceeds a single context window?
How do recursive language model systems differ from ReAct-style agents in how they handle long context?
Which methods compress a long input into a shorter representation that a language model can still use?
When does retrieval-augmented generation outperform simply feeding the whole document to a long-context model?
What benchmarks evaluate reasoning over a corpus of many documents rather than a single long document?
How is long-context recall measured, and what do needle-in-a-haystack tests fail to capture?
How do agent scaffolds implement a memory hierarchy to keep working state across many steps?
What goes wrong when an agent summarises its own context repeatedly, and how is the information loss measured?
How do papers reduce the inference cost of processing very long inputs, and how do they measure the savings?
What is context rot, and which interventions reduce the degradation of model accuracy as the context grows?
How are knowledge graphs constructed automatically from scientific papers using language models?
Which approaches extract entities and typed relations from research text without task-specific training data?
How is a systematic literature review automated, from screening papers to extracting their findings?
How is citation faithfulness of a generated answer evaluated, beyond checking that the cited document exists?
How is hallucination detected in retrieval-augmented generation when the answer cites retrieved passages?
How do cross-encoder rerankers improve passage retrieval over a first-stage dense retriever, and what do they cost?
How do dense retrieval and BM25 compare on scientific text, and when is combining them better than either alone?
How is multi-document summarisation done when the documents are long and only some are relevant?
How do long-horizon agents decide which tool to call next, and how do they recover from a failed call?
How is uncertainty estimated for a language model's answer when no ground truth is available?
Does sampling several answers and taking a majority improve accuracy, and on which tasks does it fail?
How should a long document be split into chunks for retrieval, and how does chunk size affect answer quality?
How are complex questions decomposed into sub-questions that can be answered from separate retrieved passages?
What makes retrieval over scientific literature harder than retrieval over web text, and how is that measured?
How reliable is an LLM judge when scoring answer quality, and how is its agreement with human raters reported?
